newsitem.title: south korea: Seoul 3-yr bond yields close flat, 3-mth yields up.
newsitem.headline: Seoul 3-yr bond yields close flat, 3-mth yields up.

text.p: Yields on benchmark three-year corporate bonds closed flat on Thursday despite massive new issues on relatively active buying, dealers said.
They said traders concentrated on the three-year bonds on expectations that three-month CD yields would rise.
* 3-mth CDs close at 13.10 pct vs Wednesday's 12.95
* Average overnight call rate at 13.19 pct vs 12.97
Yields on benchmark three-year corporate bonds closed unchaged on Thursday despite heavy new issues, dealers said.
They said traders concentrated on the three-year bonds on expectations that three-month CD yields would rise.
They said such expectations were based on the fact yields on three-month commercial papers have been rising steadily.
"Traders shunned CDs as they expected short-term yields to rise. Instead, they turned to three-year corporates," said Kang Yung-gee of Hyundai Securities.
The overnight call rates ranged from 12.80 percent to 13.40 percent, compared with Wednesday's average of 12.97 percent.
"Call rates gained a little as liquidity at the banking system tightened slightly," said an LG Securities broker.
New corporate bond issues totalled 201 billion won on Thursday, about four times an average daily volume.
